newsitem.title: CHINA: China approves 33 firms for B share listings.
newsitem.headline: China approves 33 firms for B share listings.

text.p: China unveiled on Tuesday a list of 33 companies that have been given approval to offer foreign currency B shares and list them on domestic stock markets.

The official Xinhua news agency said the companies were in the electric power, transport, electronics, telecommunications, petrochemicals, textiles, building materials, light industry and pharmaceutical sectors.
The list included Benxi Steel, Shenyang Petrochemical and two companies that operate highways - Hainan Expressway and Jiangxi Ganbei Expressway.
Xinhua said the companies were approved by the Securities Commission of the State Council, or cabinet.

B shares are denominated in foreign currencies and are supposed to be reserved for foreign investors. But domestic investors who have access to foreign currency are often able to buy and sell the stock, which trades on the bourses in Shanghai and southern China's Shenzhen.

The Xinhua statement also quoted a spokesman of the Securities Commission as saying that supervision of the market ought be tightened and that domestic investors ought to be banned from trading B shares.
The statement did not mention any new policy measures to enforce a ban on trading, however.
